title: The Standard Behind the Label
title_ja: ラベルの背後にある基準
fact_notes: 登場人物・活動・場所・観察結果は架空の教育事例。特定の実在の調査・製品・制度を報告するものではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A high school class was investigating how goods produced in one country could be sold in markets on the other side of the world.
sentences.ja: ある高校のクラスは一国で生産された商品が世界の反対側の市場でどう販売されるかを調べていた。

sentences.en: For their introductory exercise, the teacher prepared several fictional examples of packages carrying information about the contents, weight, and place of production.
sentences.ja: 導入活動として教師は内容、重量、生産地の情報を記載した架空の商品包装例をいくつか用意した。

sentences.en: The students noticed that the information appeared in different orders and used measurements that were not always familiar to them.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは情報の記載順が異なり、必ずしもなじみのない測定単位が使われていることに気づいた。

sentences.en: Their task was to design a label that could be understood by a group of imaginary customers in more than one country.
sentences.ja: 課題は複数の国の架空の顧客に理解されるラベルを設計することだった。

sentences.en: At first, several groups concentrated on translating all of the words on the package into a single common language.
sentences.ja: 最初、いくつかのグループは包装上の単語をすべて一つの共通言語に翻訳することに集中した。

sentences.en: They soon discovered that using the same language did not resolve every difficulty involved in comparing the information provided.
sentences.ja: 同じ言語を使っても提供された情報の比較に伴うすべての難しさが解消されないとすぐに気づいた。

sentences.en: For example, students sometimes confused whether a stated weight referred to one item or the entire contents of a package.
sentences.ja: 例えば、記載された重量が一品を指すのか包装全体の中身を指すのか混同することがあった。

sentences.en: The class discussed how shared definitions and a clear presentation of measurements could reduce the likelihood of such misunderstandings.
sentences.ja: クラスは共通の定義と明確な測定値の表示がそのような誤解の可能性をどう減らすか話し合った。

sentences.en: The next challenge was deciding which pieces of information should appear in the most prominent positions on the proposed label.
sentences.ja: 次の課題はどの情報を提案ラベルの最も目立つ位置に表示すべきか決めることだった。

sentences.en: The imaginary customers included people who wanted to compare prices quickly, people who needed to check ingredients, and people unfamiliar with the product.
sentences.ja: 架空の顧客には価格をすばやく比較したい人、原材料を確認する必要がある人、製品に不慣れな人が含まれていた。

sentences.en: Rather than assuming that every customer would read the entire package carefully, the groups developed a consistent order for essential information.
sentences.ja: すべての顧客が包装全体を丁寧に読むと思い込まず、重要情報の一貫した表示順を考えた。

sentences.en: They then tested their proposed designs by asking other students to locate particular facts without being told where to look.
sentences.ja: 次に、どこを見るか教えず特定の情報を探してもらい、提案デザインを検証した。

sentences.en: After comparing the results, the students recognized that adopting a shared format could make some information easier to locate across different products.
sentences.ja: 結果を比較すると、共通の形式を採用すれば異なる製品間で情報を見つけやすくなる場合があると認識した。

sentences.en: However, a single format could not automatically address every local language requirement or every possible need of a customer.
sentences.ja: しかし一つの形式ですべての地域言語の要件や顧客のあらゆる必要性に自動的に対応できるわけではなかった。

sentences.en: The class therefore proposed a common structure for the main information while allowing space for additional explanations adapted to particular audiences.
sentences.ja: そこで主要情報には共通構造を提案しつつ、特定の読み手に合わせた補足説明の余地を設けた。

sentences.en: The teacher emphasized that the classroom design was an educational example, not a substitute for checking actual labeling requirements in a particular market.
sentences.ja: 教師は教室のデザインは教育用の例であり、特定市場の実際の表示要件の確認に代わるものではないと強調した。

sentences.en: The exercise helped the students understand that international exchange depends partly on the ability of people in different places to interpret information consistently.
sentences.ja: 活動は国際的な取引が異なる場所の人々が情報を一貫して解釈できる能力にも左右されることを理解する助けになった。

sentences.en: A shared standard can make communication simpler, but its usefulness depends on whether it addresses the actual uncertainty people experience.
sentences.ja: 共通基準は意思疎通を簡単にできるが、その有用性は人々が実際に経験する不確実さに対処するかに左右される。

sentences.en: Local differences do not disappear simply because participants agree to use a common format for certain information.
sentences.ja: 特定情報に共通形式を使うと参加者が同意したからといって地域差がなくなるわけではない。

sentences.en: For the class, meaningful cooperation involved identifying what could be standardized and what needed to remain flexible.
sentences.ja: クラスにとって意義ある協力とは、標準化できるものと柔軟に保つ必要があるものを見極めることだった。

options: The students were unable to translate any words.
Every package used exactly the same measurements.
Customers preferred packages with no text.
Shared language did not remove uncertainty about what measurements referred to.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ言語でも重量などが指す内容が曖昧になり得た。

options: The weight of one item and that of the whole contents.
The name of the teacher and the name of the school.
The countries where all students lived.
The color of the label and the product's shape.
questions.explanation_ja: 一品か中身全体かを混同した。

questions.prompt: How did the groups test the designs?
options: They asked teachers to memorize every package.
They asked other students to find facts without giving their locations.
They printed all information in the smallest font.
They removed all measurements from every label.
questions.explanation_ja: 場所を教えず情報を探してもらった。

questions.prompt: Why did the groups arrange essential information consistently?
options: Every customer had exactly the same purpose.
The students wanted to hide the ingredients.
All fictional packages had identical contents.
Not every customer would read the entire package carefully.
questions.explanation_ja: 全体を読むとは限らないため重要情報の順序を揃えた。

questions.prompt: What did the class propose after examining the results?
options: A shared structure with room for locally adapted explanations.
A single unchangeable design for every possible market.
An end to all common product information.
A ban on mentioning ingredients.
questions.explanation_ja: 共通構造と個別の補足説明を組み合わせた。

options: A feature added for decoration.
A type of package weight.
Something used in place of another.
A statement showing disagreement.

questions.prompt: What limitation of common standards does the author identify?
options: They do not eliminate all local differences or uncertainty on their own.
They can never make information easier to compare.
They require every participant to live in the same country.
They always make products more expensive.
questions.explanation_ja: 共通形式だけで地域差や不確実性は消えない。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the central argument?
options: Every country should use exactly the same label in all circumstances.
Translation alone guarantees successful international trade.
Local differences make any shared information impossible.
International cooperation can combine shared standards with flexibility for different needs.
questions.explanation_ja: 共通の基準と柔軟性の両立。

paraphrases.source: A high school class was investigating how goods produced in one country could be sold in markets on the other side of the world.
paraphrases.rewrite: The class studied how products made in one nation might reach buyers in distant countries.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 一国の製品が遠い国の買い手に届く仕組みを調べた。

paraphrases.source: They soon discovered that using the same language did not resolve every difficulty involved in comparing the information provided.
paraphrases.rewrite: They found that sharing a language could still leave problems when people tried to compare information.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 共通言語だけでは比較の問題が残る。

paraphrases.source: Rather than assuming that every customer would read the entire package carefully, the groups developed a consistent order for essential information.
paraphrases.rewrite: The groups did not expect everyone to read every detail; instead, they arranged key information consistently.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 全員が細部まで読むと仮定せず重要情報を整えた。

paraphrases.source: Local differences do not disappear simply because participants agree to use a common format for certain information.
paraphrases.rewrite: Agreement on a common format for selected information is not enough to remove local differences.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 一部の共通形式への合意だけで地域差はなくならない。
